editorial.meta_description: The BCIDP Infectious Disease Pharmacist exam evaluates the clinical knowledge, therapeutic management skills, and professional practice standards required.
editorial.overview: The BCIDP Infectious Disease Pharmacist certification is administered by the Board of Pharmacy Specialties. This exam evaluates a pharmacist's knowledge across three primary domains: Pathophysiology and Epidemiology of Infections, Therapeutics and Patient Management, and Professional Practice. It ensures that practitioners demonstrate the necessary expertise to manage complex infectious disease cases and contribute to effective patient care outcomes in various clinical settings. The certification process validates the professional skills required to navigate the challenges of modern infectious disease pharmacy practice effectively and maintain high standards of care.
editorial.who_should_take: This certification is for pharmacists who manage infectious diseases in clinical practice. Candidates should have experience in patient management, therapeutic decision-making, and the application of epidemiological principles to improve health outcomes for patients with various infections.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review the three domains to align your study with the exam weights. Focus 60.0% of your effort on Therapeutics and Patient Management, as it is the largest section. Use the official Board of Pharmacy Specialties exam guide to understand the scope of the 150 questions. Practice applying clinical knowledge to patient cases to prepare for the 225-minute testing period. Ensure you are familiar with all domain requirements to succeed in your certification goals.

domain_guidance.summary: This domain covers the biological mechanisms of infections and the important patterns of disease spread within populations, accounting for exactly 18.0% of the total exam content for all candidates seeking certification.

This domain focuses on clinical decision-making and patient care strategies, representing 60.0% of the exam, which makes it the primary area of assessment for candidates seeking to demonstrate their professional expertise in pharmacy.

This domain addresses the professional responsibilities and practice standards required of an infectious disease pharmacist, comprising 22.0% of the overall examination content to ensure high quality care for all patients in clinical settings.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: You will have 225 minutes to complete 150 questions. Manage your time effectively across the three domains to ensure you address all sections. Read each question to identify the specific therapeutic or epidemiological focus required for the correct answer.

faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?
faq.answer_text: The BCIDP Infectious Disease Pharmacist exam consists of 150 questions in total. These questions are distributed across three domains, with the largest portion focused on Therapeutics and Patient Management for all test takers.

Information regarding the specific passing score for this certification is not provided in the current documentation. Please check with the Board of Pharmacy Specialties for details on scoring requirements and certification maintenance.

The total duration for the BCIDP Infectious Disease Pharmacist exam is 225 minutes. Candidates should plan their time to address the 150 questions within this period to ensure they complete every section.

The BCIDP Infectious Disease Pharmacist certification is granted by the Board of Pharmacy Specialties. They maintain the standards and official documentation for this current certification and provide all necessary guidance for candidates.
